s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove with localized linear hair loss and hair thinning on the scalp and forehead
salient_findings: Arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the left side of the forehead, frontal scalp, and vertex area
Localized linear hair loss and hair thinning on the left scalp area
Presence of short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation on dermoscopic examination
key_facts: The patient is a man in his 50s
The lesion began approximately 10 years earlier
The patient received 2 doses of intralesional steroid via injection on a small bald patch on the vertex
The lesion gradually progressed to the frontal scalp and eventually made a linear furrow on the left side of the forehead
The patient denied any trauma history
The patient had no history of connective tissue disease
No evidence of systemic involvement, such as arthralgia, photosensitivity, or skin rashes
Dermoscopic examination revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
The result of a hair pull test was negative
Histopathologic examination showed predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis
Direct immunofluorescence was positive with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of an asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the left side of his forehead, frontal scalp, and vertex area, along with localized linear hair loss and hair thinning, is consistent with Scleroderma en coup de sabre. The histopathologic examination showing lymphocytic infiltrates and lobular panniculitis, as well as the positive direct immunofluorescence, also support this diagnosis. The gradual progression of the lesion over 10 years and the absence of systemic involvement or trauma history further point towards Scleroderma en coup de sabre.

rejected.label: Frontal fibrosing alopecia
rejected.why: While frontal fibrosing alopecia can cause hair loss and scarring, it typically does not present with a depressed skin groove or linear furrow.

rejected.label: Lichen planopilaris
rejected.why: Lichen planopilaris can cause hair loss and inflammation, but it is not typically associated with a depressed skin groove or linear furrow, and the histopathologic findings do not match.

rejected.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: Discoid lupus erythematosus can cause hair loss and scarring, but the patient's negative antinuclear antibody and lack of systemic involvement make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Linear morphoea
rejected.why: While linear morphoea can cause a linear, depressed skin lesion, the patient's presentation and histopathologic findings are more consistent with Scleroderma en coup de sabre.

gold: Linear or annular lupus erythematosus panniculitis of the scalp (LALPS)
